meaningfulUpdates.title: In re Dwight York, No. 25-11486 (11th Cir.)
meaningfulUpdates.summary: York sought Eleventh Circuit authorization to file a successive Section 2255 motion based on asserted newly discovered evidence of factual innocence. The court denied authorization on May 19, 2025. A panel-rehearing petition was filed June 2; the clerk stated June 3 that no action would be taken because reconsideration is not permitted in a successive habeas proceeding under 11th Cir. R. 22-3(b).
missingEvidence: Full text of May 1 emergency application
Full text of May 19 Eleventh Circuit order
notes: Docket metadata establishes filing and disposition, not the truth of the factual-innocence allegations.

meaningfulUpdates.title: York v. Macon County Police Department, No. 5:25-cv-00507-CAR-CHW (M.D. Ga.)
meaningfulUpdates.summary: York filed a pro se habeas petition on November 18, 2025. The magistrate judge recommended dismissal as an unauthorized second or successive Section 2255 motion; Judge C. Ashley Royal adopted the recommendation and dismissed without prejudice for lack of jurisdiction on December 18, 2025, denying a certificate of appealability. Judgment entered December 22. Mail containing the order and judgment was returned as undeliverable on January 21, 2026.
missingEvidence: Full text of the November 18 petition is not publicly mirrored in the sources located during this run.
notes: The returned mail is procedurally notable but does not by itself establish a due-process violation; service history would need fuller docket review.

meaningfulUpdates.title: Medical-diagnosis contradiction relevant to compassionate release
meaningfulUpdates.summary: A 2018 District of Colorado order on GovInfo records that BOP testing and the summary-judgment record treated York's condition as idiopathic angioedema/urticaria rather than hereditary angioedema; the order also noted York's expert view that idiopathic angioedema can be potentially life-threatening. Current 2026 media reports describe York's February 13 compassionate-release filing as asserting hereditary angioedema. The April 7, 2026 M.D. Georgia order confirms a pending compassionate-release motion and counsel-status issue but does not resolve the diagnosis.
missingEvidence: The February 13, 2026 compassionate-release motion and current medical exhibits are needed to determine whether later testing changed the diagnosis or whether the filing uses a disputed historical diagnosis.
notes: Do not treat the 2018 order as a timeless medical diagnosis; later evidence could supersede it.
Do not treat a media paraphrase of the 2026 motion as proof of the present diagnosis.
